items.headline: Nvidia's board reinstates its CEO on Nov 23, eleven days after he resigned
items.why: Leadership at the largest AI-chip supplier is back to the pre-resignation status quo, but the reinstatement came with political pressure attached, so the regulatory overhang on the stock is not resolved.

items.headline: Congress lines up chip-export scrutiny: Senate Banking hearing Dec 3, Commerce Secretary invited Dec 10
items.why: A Nov 16 Commerce rule already requires licenses for advanced chips going to overseas data centers serving China-headquartered firms, and Democratic leaders are pushing for tighter limits, so export policy is the live risk for AI-chip revenue into December.

items.headline: Bitcoin trades near $60,600 on Nov 26, up about 3% in 24 hours, with more than $5 billion of November spot-ETF outflows
items.why: The bounce is happening against heavy fund selling, which is why one analyst firm called it fragile: price is rising without the ETF demand that drove earlier advances.

items.headline: About $7 billion of bitcoin options expire on Deribit on Nov 27, put/call open-interest ratio 0.89
items.why: Large expiries can pin or jolt spot price around the settlement time; a ratio below 1 means calls slightly outnumber puts, so the positioning is not a one-sided bearish bet.

items.headline: October core PCE hits 3.3% a year, above the 3.2% expected; Q3 GDP revised up to 4.3%; December Fed hike priced near 94%
items.why: Hotter inflation plus stronger growth removes the argument for holding at the Dec 8-9 meeting, so markets now treat a quarter-point hike as the base case rather than a risk.

items.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield rises about 8 basis points to roughly 4.93% on Nov 27
items.why: Yields climbing into a likely hike keeps pressure on long-duration assets such as growth stocks and gold, even on a day equities rallied.

items.headline: Gold rises 1.94% to about $3,637 an ounce on Nov 27, still roughly a third below its Jan 28 high near $5,400
items.why: The bounce is small against the drawdown, so gold has not yet recovered its role as the hedge it was earlier this year while rate-hike odds stay high.

items.headline: WTI crude falls 1.7% to $82.69 on Nov 27; Brent quoted near $96.60 intraday
items.why: Oil is still elevated, which keeps inflation pressure alive for the Fed, though the one-day drop shows the price is not moving in a straight line.

items.headline: S&P 500 closes the holiday-shortened session at 7,297 (+1.60%); Nasdaq Composite 24,129 (+2.31%); Dow 50,775 (+1.18%)
items.why: The index finished well above its 7,263 level at the open, so buyers held and extended the gain through the session, but it was a half-day on thin volume and one session does not make a trend.

items.headline: Breadth is wide: Russell 2000 +1.71% to 2,750, and ten of 11 S&P sectors were up at midday
items.why: A rally led by small caps and nearly every sector is broader than a tech-only bounce, which makes it more durable than the headline index move alone suggests.
